$comment: Example configuration for multi-instance development. Copy to multi-instance.config.json (or point $ACME_WORKTREE_CONFIG at your own copy) and edit paths/apps. The registry under .instances is managed by the acme-worktree CLI — keys are worktree NAMES, i.e. the directory name with paths.worktreePrefix stripped.

acme.description: Primary development instance (reserved — slot 1 is the main repo and is never freed)

portAllocation.$comment: Port = base + (instance - 1). One integer per worktree therefore derives every port, so nothing collides. Bases must stay further apart than maxInstances: backend 3000 and domainApi 3200 are 200 apart, so they would overlap at instance 201.

defaults.$comment: maxInstances is the allocator ceiling: create fails with 'No available instance numbers' once every slot from 2..maxInstances is taken. Raise it only if the port bases above stay further apart than the new ceiling. Instance 1 uses primaryDbName; every other instance gets dbNamePrefix + the worktree name with hyphens turned into underscores. domainApiDbUser/Name are used ONLY to compose a DATABASE_URL template when the domain API has no .env yet — an existing DATABASE_URL never has its credentials rewritten, only its host:port.

paths.$comment: A leading ~ is expanded when the config is read. Non-primary worktrees live at <worktreeRoot>/<worktreePrefix><name>; mainRepo's own directory name is the registry key of the primary instance (here: acme).

apps.$comment: Repo-relative app directories. Each is optional: a generated file is only written when its directory exists in the worktree, so a consumer with two of these four still works.
